name: Reef Caustics
description: The product settled into the rippled white sand of a shallow reef shelf, a live caustic net sliding across the sand and up over its curvature, suspended particulate hanging through the water column. Real submersion and real refraction — the surface stays above the frame.
lighting: Hard sun through surface chop, moving caustic net
subject: product
prompt: a frosted sea-glass-green bottle with a brushed metal collar, the product is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 55 percent of the frame height, tack-sharp, settled into the white carbonate sand of a shallow underwater reef shelf, the product lit to read as a solid three-dimensional volume, its own form shading falling off toward both silhouette edges with the brightest band down its centre, a narrow core shadow inside one edge and a thin bright rim where the surface turns away at the other, never evenly bright from edge to edge, the caustic net breaking over that curvature, its cells wide and open only across the centre band and stretching, skewing and compressing into narrow slivers as they approach each silhouette, never a flat even pattern laid across the body, on the seabed the same net landing as bright wavering polygons, cells large and open in the near foreground and shrinking steadily with distance to fine sparkle at the coral line so the light reads on a receding floor rather than on a wall, the sand worked into real parallel ripple bars running away from camera with crests catching light and troughs holding blue shadow and the bar spacing tightening toward the back of frame, a soft scour hollow dug in around the base, hard sun almost overhead and slightly behind throwing one short dark cast shadow forward onto the sand toward camera with a brighter refracted halo ringing its edge, the base meeting the sand along a hard contact line with no gap, defined light shafts cutting through suspended particulate, a scatter of adhering micro-bubbles across the upper surfaces, the pale sand bouncing a weak uplight into the underside only without flattening the side-to-side falloff, low mounded coral heads and soft gorgonian fans held at the frame edges in muted rose and ochre, softened by real visibility falloff into blue-green haze, colour running from bright aquamarine in the near water to deep teal at distance against bleached white sand, correct underwater colour absorption with reds dropping out at distance, no flat sticker-like caustic overlay, no water surface or mirrored ceiling in frame, no fish or marine life, no tank wall or pool edge, no diving equipment, no second product, immaculate high-end commercial clarity
